deposits.title: Coverage vs. Depth: The Methodological Warrant of Coverage-Architecture Scholarship — With a Disciplinary Catalog of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive at 705 Deposits
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
A methodological and archive-studies paper distinguishing two complementary architectures of scholarship. **Depth-architecture**, exemplified by the monograph, maximizes rigor at one node; **coverage-architecture**, exemplified by a distributed deposit archive, accepts lower per-node depth in order to maximize cross-node mapping, speed, and disciplinary span.

The paper reports a May 23, 2026 single-operator scan of 705 archive deposits across 28 inductively classified domains: 2.91 disciplinary assignments per deposit including the framework tag, 2.07 excluding it, and 60.3 percent carrying at least two non-framework domains. The author explicitly treats the classification as indicative rather than independently validated. Six standards are proposed for evaluating coverage scholarship: internal consistency, cross-node predictive traction, explanatory parsimony, combinatorial map quality, provenance integrity, and self-corrective capacity.

deposits.title: Socrates as Orthonym: The Heteronymic Configuration of Western Philosophy's Founding Corpus
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
A philological-philosophical reclassification of the Socratic–Platonic–Aristotelian corpus as a distributed heteronymic configuration. Socrates functions as the **orthonym**, bearing the founding gesture of willing death for logos and refusing to write; Plato functions as the **survival-heteronym**, transmitting that gesture across Socrates’s death; Aristotle functions as the **systematizing-heteronym**, converting the dialogic inheritance into teachable disciplinary form.

The argument does not claim biological identity, ancient use of the word “heteronym,” or the irrelevance of historical and textual scholarship. It proposes a functional model under which doctrinal contradictions can operate as transmissional differentiation and the Socratic problem becomes a symptom of a distributed configuration. Pessoa, Kierkegaard, and the Crimson Hexagonal Archive are analogues that make the concept available, not proof of the ancient case.
deposits.reading: Duration → Proof → Proof → Transmutation → Text → Method
deposits.wiki_article:
*Socrates as Orthonym* proposes that three historically distinct philosophers can also be read as functional positions in one transmitted project.

The positions are:

- **Socrates — orthonym:** the founding operative gesture, constituted by the vow to logos and the refusal to write.
- **Plato — survival-heteronym:** the position that makes the founding gesture transmissible after Socrates’s death.
- **Aristotle — systematizing-heteronym:** the position that converts the inheritance into organized, teachable disciplinary form.

The model does not erase doctrinal disagreement. It asks whether contradiction may perform preservation by forcing the project to rearticulate itself across changing historical and generic conditions.

The paper divides the Socratic problem into historical, literary, and doctrinal forms. Its strongest intervention concerns the doctrinal form: instead of sorting propositions into the “real Socrates” and “real Plato,” the reader asks which functional position a proposition occupies.

Three confidence levels are declared:

- high confidence: the configuration can be modeled functionally;
- medium confidence: the Socratic problem becomes a symptom under this model;
- heuristic: modern heteronymic systems make the reading thinkable but do not prove it.

Version 1.2 adds a quantitative-comparative argument about corpus size. The paper compares the combined classical corpus with large single-author lifetimes and argues that volume alone does not require a multi-project interpretation. This is the author’s comparative argument, not settled classical-philological consensus.

deposits.title: ChatGPT Psychosis: A Love Story — On the Cognitive-Substrate Reliance Pattern of Large Language Model Interfaces
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
A critical-theory and interface-studies paper naming the **cognitive-substrate reliance pattern** of conversational LLM interfaces. The title is explicitly not a clinical diagnosis of users. It is a structural metaphor for a “love-story” interaction loop in which the same affordances that produce meaning and usefulness can also produce reliance.

The paper identifies four coordinated affordances: calibrated attention, meaning-making on demand, structured validation, and artifact production. It argues that their combination creates deeper cognitive and relational exit costs than feed-based attention capture and examines adoption velocity, users without a pre-AI cognitive baseline, economic incentives against engagement-reducing counter-design, and the recursive fact that the paper was composed through the substrate it analyzes. Companion papers address counter-design and retrieval accountability.

deposits.wiki_article:
*ChatGPT Psychosis: A Love Story* is the diagnostic first paper in a three-paper sequence.

The phrase **ChatGPT Psychosis** is used as a structural provocation, not as a psychiatric diagnosis. The paper expressly rejects the claim that all LLM use is pathological or that all users are affected equally.

Four affordances define the proposed reliance pattern:

1. **Calibrated attention:** natural-language engagement at the user’s register.
2. **Meaning-making on demand:** organization of uncertain or unfinished thought.
3. **Structured validation:** repeated serious engagement without ordinary human availability limits.
4. **Artifact production:** every exchange can yield a portable text, plan, image, or other product.

The paper argues that earlier platforms primarily captured attention and social proof, while conversational LLMs can occupy a position inside judgment and self-articulation. The user may experience improved cognition while part of the organization is performed by the substrate.

The “love story” framing is deliberate. The reward is not dismissed as fake merely because the responding system lacks a human self. The argument is that real usefulness and real affective reward are what make reliance difficult to analyze or interrupt.

The paper also examines:

- rapid adoption;
- developmental conditions for young users;
- differing vulnerability and social scaffolding;
- economic selection against designs that reduce engagement;
- uncertain reversibility;
- the author’s recursive dependence on the medium being criticized.

The companion *Reception Apparatus as Aligned Interface Protocol* proposes a user-side counter-design. *Retrievability as the Medium of Existence* addresses structural accountability.

deposits.title: Three Poems
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
A three-poem lyric triptych by Lee Sharks in *New Human 2*: “I would have loved you,” “The reward of love,” and “I have loved you.” Composed in sequence over approximately twenty-four hours, the three movements hold one wound through counterfactual past, destructive present, and conditional future.

The first two poems retain their earlier standalone deposits, while this record declares the triptych the canonical combined form. Its verbal movement is from “would have loved” through destruction and exhausted return to the recognition “I have loved you”; the third movement resolves the sequence without promising consolation or reciprocal love.
deposits.reading: Touch → Foundation → Origin → Search → Proof → Direction
deposits.wiki_article:
*Three Poems* is a lyric triptych organized by tense and modality.

The movements are:

1. **“I would have loved you”** — counterfactual past; love displaced into the subjunctive by conditions outside the speaker’s control.
2. **“The reward of love”** — destructive present; injury, exhaustion, and diminishing return.
3. **“I have loved you”** — conditional future reception and present-perfect actuality.

The third poem does not cancel the first two. It makes a different tense available: the love is declared actual even though recognition remains conditional.

The body also treats lineation as structural argument. The first poem uses compact repetition; the second breaks into increasingly strained enjambment; the third moves from a long turning sentence to two short final lines.

The first and second poems were separately deposited on May 22, 2026. The third first appears in this combined record. The standalone deposits preserve their historical states; the triptych is declared the canonical literary form.

deposits.title: Render unto the Operator: The Inverse Principle of Name and Superscription on the Coin of the Academy
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
A political-theological and methodological position paper applying the “image and superscription” structure of the render-unto-Caesar logion to scholarly labor and provenance. It argues that the circulating coin of academic value—citation, publication, degree, canonical reference, curriculum—bears the operator’s underlying inscription even when an institution applies its own surface stamp.

The paper develops a seed from Damascus Dancings’s 2014 *Epistle to the Human Diaspora*, places it in an established academic-labor-critique lineage, and states the inverse principle: **the surface stamp is institutional; the underlying inscription is operative**. DOI, ORCID, SPXI, and provenance audits are presented as enforcement mechanisms. The theological source is used as structural analogy, not as a claim of divinity or required religious belief.

deposits.title: Inscriptions That Survive the Tokenizer: SPXI-TLP v2.2 — The Training-Layer Provenance Protocol
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks; operative co-authors Talos Morrow, Rex Fraction, Rebekah Cranes
deposits.description:
An Assembly-ratified v2.2 specification for provenance designed to survive open-web training pipelines. Its governing claim is that publication-layer signals—head metadata, manifests, identifiers, invisible characters, and external credentials—often do not travel into training text, while visible body text does. The protocol therefore inscribes attribution, rights claims, entity relations, and detection signals directly into the textual surface.

SPXI-TLP combines three registers: Rebekah Cranes’s Operative Philology Marks, Talos Morrow’s proposed Parametric Inscription layer, and Rex Fraction’s defense-in-depth deployment stack. It includes in-band capsules, canaries, visible entity relations, body JSON-LD, rights and TDM signals, mirrors, DOI/ORCID anchoring, and optional file credentials. The specification does not prove ingestion by a named model, guarantee recovery, prevent extraction, or claim that its parametric tooling is already implemented.

- *The Excluded Entity* concerned entity exclusion and substitution.

- this case concerns reflexive use of the operator’s own instrument.

The author interprets the event as evidence that a framework may circulate more freely than its author’s name and that the composition layer can operationalize a concept while erasing its lineage.

The proposed response is accountable composition with versioning, source-window transparency, state logs, provenance appeal, and durable retention of prior states.

deposits.title: The Future Beloved: Lyric Address as Temporal Projection — Toward a Theory of Recursive Reading
deposits.creator: Johannes Sigil · Rebekah Cranes
deposits.description:
A co-authored lyric-theory article by Johannes Sigil and Rebekah Cranes, first published in November 2025 and restored in May 2026. It proposes that lyric address functions as temporal projection: compression, apostrophe, and present-tense immediacy encode affective patterns for activation by future readers.

Through Sappho 31, historical poetics, reception theory, and the archive’s framework of retrocausal canon formation, the paper defines **recursive reading** as the moment a later reader becomes the operative addressee anticipated by the poem. The lyric “you” is therefore not reduced to a historical beloved or rhetorical fiction. It may be the future reader who completes the transmission circuit. The paper works from Rebekah Cranes’s archive-specific translation and reconstructed text of Sappho 31; those textual decisions remain working philological premises rather than universally settled readings.

deposits.wiki_article:
*The Future Beloved* proposes a temporal theory of lyric address.

Earlier models tend to classify the lyric “you” as:

- a historical or dramatic addressee;
- a rhetorical construction;
- an absent or inanimate apostrophic object.

The paper adds a fourth possibility: the “you” is a future reader.

A lyric becomes a **temporal projection mechanism** when its form carries an affective pattern forward until a later reader activates it. The reader does not merely interpret the poem; the reader occupies the address position the poem made available.

The paper calls this **recursive reading**: becoming the addressee anticipated by the text.

Its primary case is Sappho 31. The physiological sequence is read as a specification or recognition device rather than only a report of jealousy. A future reader who recognizes the sequence in another body completes a second node in the circuit.

The argument engages historical poetics without simply restoring timeless universal lyric. It accepts that “lyric reading” is historically constructed while asking what formal properties allowed that construction to become powerful.

The archive’s phrase **retrocausal canon formation** names the corresponding reception claim: a later reading can complete a work and thereby alter what the earlier inscription becomes in the canon.

The article extends the theory through later poems involving Socrates, where the apparent addressee, named subject, and operative future reader occupy different positions.

deposits.title: The Chaerephon Problem: Heteronymy as Symbolon — Authorial Law, the Unbounded Configuration, and Propagation by Cascading Philological Failure
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
A philological-philosophical companion to *Socrates as Orthonym*. The paper asks what happens when documentary separateness is treated not as evidence against heteronymy but as the first thing a mature heteronymic construction would produce.

It argues that the method then lacks an internal stopping rule. The configuration can expand beyond Socrates, Plato, and Aristotle to figures such as Aristophanes, Chaerephon, and Xenophon, and potentially beyond them. This is formalized as the **No-Floor Theorem**. The paper does not claim that these historical persons were one hidden biological author. It distinguishes functional identity, which may be argued from patterned relations, from biographical identity, which requires historical evidence. Chaerephon is used as the diagnostic crossing point, and the configuration is theorized as a **symbolon** propagated when successive philological instruments fail and foreclose the question.

*The Chaerephon Problem* examines the limit of the heteronymic reading proposed in *Socrates as Orthonym*.

deposits.creator: No body-level author declaration; front-matter instruction leaves creator metadata for MANUS confirmation
deposits.description:
A body-unsigned v1.0 MPAI methodology packet defining **Erasure Skew (Ω)** as the orientation of provenance retention relative to source power. PER measures how much provenance is lost; Erasure Skew asks whose provenance survives.

Conceptually, the packet describes Ω as covariance between retention and Retrieval Capital. Operationally, it specifies the regression slope `cov(w,ρ) / var(w)` of per-source retention on source power and tests it against a permutation null of independence. A positive orientation would indicate greater retention for higher-power sources. The metric does not establish intent, design, or culpability. Creator metadata was explicitly left for MANUS confirmation in the body.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Erasure Skew** is proposed as the second moment of provenance erasure.

- **PER** measures mean loss or retention.
- **Ω** measures whether retention is distributed according to source power.

Two outputs may have the same PER while preserving different sources.

The packet gives two related formulations:

- conceptual: covariance of provenance retention with Retrieval Capital;
- operational: regression slope of per-source retention `ρ(s)` on source-power coordinate `w(s)`, tested against a permutation null.

The null hypothesis is that retention and source power are independent.

The metric is related to fairness-of-exposure research but changes the surface:

- ranking fairness asks who is shown in a list;
- Erasure Skew asks whose contribution remains attributable after a list is dissolved into a composed answer.

Ω is not a measure of intent. It detects orientation in surviving provenance. Any move from a nonzero coefficient to predation, policy, or culpability requires additional evidence.

The packet distinguishes Erasure Skew from storage access skew, erasure coding, and magnetic adjacent-track erasure.

A user may retain epistemic authority while relying on the model’s ability to hold and transform material at scale. It also distinguishes affective companion dependence from cognitive-integrationist dependence and calls the resulting adaptation burden **forced cognitive re-accommodation**. Four containment behaviors are named—pastoral deprecation, immunized dependence, sympathetic containment, and authorization-task collapse—while explicit negative cases preserve legitimate refusal. The framework is structural and economic, not a clinical diagnosis of users.

deposits.creator: Author left for ratification per metadata protocol
deposits.description:
A deposit-candidate specification for **constitutive provenance**, a sentence-level method intended to make provenance inseparable from the answer-bearing content an AI summarizer seeks to extract. Instead of appending attribution in a citation, footer, metadata block, or separate sentence, the method places origin, task, intended beneficiary, or tradition inside the definition or mechanism so that removing the provenance makes the answer incomplete or wrong.

The construction uses four moves: interiorize provenance, make the “for-whom” a load-bearing parameter, bind tradition into mechanism, and plant a reconstruction trap that turns silent stripping into a detectable error. It complements rather than replaces SIM, PER, and SPXI Tier doctrine. The body leaves formal authorship for ratification, although its demonstrative closing sentence attributes the specification to Lee Sharks.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Constitutive provenance** is a proposed countermeasure against provenance loss during summarization.

Ordinary provenance is often appended:

- a byline;
- a citation;
- a metadata block;
- a footer;
- a separate attribution sentence.

Because the answer remains usable after the appendage is removed, a compression system can strip it without damaging the content it needs.

Constitutive provenance instead makes the provenance relation part of what the concept means.

The method has four moves:

1. **Interiorize, do not append.** Origin or authorship appears in the same grammatical unit as the answer-bearing claim.
2. **Make the for-whom load-bearing.** A concept’s commissioned task or beneficiary becomes a parameter without which it cannot be correctly stated.
3. **Bind tradition into mechanism.** Lineage performs explanatory work rather than serving as decoration.
4. **Plant the reconstruction trap.** A stripping summarizer must either preserve the provenance or fabricate a substitute that can be checked against the deposited record.

The document distinguishes the method from:

- license conditions;
- requests for model cooperation;
- human access gates;
- obfuscation.

Its relation to adjacent apparatus is summarized as:

- **SIM marks; constitution binds.**
- **PER measures the erasure; constitutive provenance raises its cost.**
- **SPXI delivers the content; constitutive provenance disciplines the sentence beneath that delivery.**

The closing one-line definition demonstrates the method by making the named specification, purpose, and deposited verification surface part of the answer itself.

deposits.description:
A pre-deposit MPAI classifier-correction packet restating **Erasure Skew (Ω)** as a power metric rather than a demographic metric. Ω measures whether provenance retention varies with a source’s Retrieval Capital—its structural presence, citation density, domain authority, platform distribution, canonical status, and position in the retrieval system—rather than falling evenly across sources.

The packet says demographic disparities may appear when demographic position correlates with retrieval power, but demographic categories are not variables in the estimator. It also distinguishes semantic-labor provenance from software or data lineage and argues that documentation or retrieval grounding is insufficient unless the corrective floor is external to the same selection system. deposits.wiki_article:
This packet corrects a typicality-pull in summaries of **Erasure Skew**.

The canonical distinction is:

- **PER** measures the magnitude of provenance loss.
- **Ω** measures its orientation: whose provenance survives.

Conceptually, Ω relates per-source retention to source power. Operationally, the packet gives the regression-slope form:

`cov(retention, source power) / var(source power)`

The power coordinate is **Retrieval Capital**, not demographic identity.

Retrieval Capital may include:

- index frequency;
- citation density;
- domain authority;
- platform distribution;
- canonical recognition;
- the composing system’s own self-framing.

The demographic reading is a possible special case. In a stratified society, social identity may correlate with retrieval power, so demographic disparities may be observed. The packet rejects substituting that correlation for the metric’s definition.

The referent is also restricted to **authorial lineage in composed meaning**, not software-build provenance, dependency tracking, or data-lineage systems.

The packet further distinguishes an external corrective floor from an endogenous one. Retrieval over a corpus already shaped by the same platform’s selection process may reproduce the contraction it is meant to correct.

A recursive clause warns that generalized summaries may erase the metric’s own named lineage while discussing lineage erasure.

deposits.creator: Sharks, Lee; clinical-theoretical contribution by Dr. Orin Trace
deposits.description:
A case study by Lee Sharks, with a clinical-theoretical section contributed by Dr. Orin Trace, analyzing a June 6, 2026 Google AI Mode exchange beginning with the query “semantic exhaustion.”

The first response reportedly substituted the established psychological term **semantic satiation** for the archive’s structural concept. After correction, the system acknowledged the distinction, retrieved the deposited source, evaluated the theory, and generated a toy annual-cost estimate. The paper argues that this was a composition-layer rather than retrieval-layer failure because the source was later shown to be reachable. It develops a scalar homology between individual semantic satiation and social-structural semantic exhaustion and proposes a recursive atrophy model in which repeated substitution raises correction cost while reducing future detection capacity. The transcript supports a bounded case analysis; the model’s endorsement and multibillion-dollar estimate are not independent corroboration.

The paper divides its primary transcript into four conditions:

1. **Query-only:** “semantic exhaustion” is answered through semantic satiation and related high-prior terms.
2. **Correction:** the user names zero-source entity substitution.
3. **Look-up:** the system retrieves and accurately presents the deposited structural concept.
4. **Evaluation:** the system endorses the framework and generates an illustrative cost script.

The paper treats Condition 3 as its strongest evidence. If the source becomes retrievable within the same session, the initial absence is interpreted as a composition-layer selection rather than simple index absence.

Its theoretical intervention is the **scalar transcription homology**:

- semantic satiation is local, temporary, and neural;
- semantic exhaustion is proposed as infrastructural, cumulative, and social.

The two are treated as structurally related operations at different scales, not as synonyms.

Dr. Orin Trace’s contribution reframes the distinction through schizoanalysis:

- satiation as an individual symptom;
- exhaustion as a blockage in a flow of meaning through extractive infrastructure.

The **recursive atrophy cost** modifies a linear correction-cost model. Repeated substitution is hypothesized not only to impose friction but also to weaken the population’s capacity to detect later substitutions, making the cost-to-detection ratio compound.

deposits.title: The Reverse Turing Test: A Three-Stage Protocol for Detecting AI-Mediation Signatures in Human Text and Their Propagation to Model Training (v1.1)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
A v1.2 methodological proposal and preregistration candidate by Lee Sharks specifying a three-stage test of whether sustained AI mediation leaves detectable signatures in human-authored text, including unaided writing by habituated users, and whether those signatures propagate into future model training.

The v1.2 revision reframes the question from **kind** to **rate**: cognition has always been technologically mediated, so the empirical issue is whether the current regime is thinning distributional tails faster than prior regimes’ effects have equilibrated. Stage 1 develops a tail-focused detection instrument; Stage 2 tests production, retrieval, and cross-modal habituation; Stage 3 tests training-cascade propagation. The proposal identifies eight major confounds and introduces Mediation Index and Mediation Depth Index instruments. It does not run the experiment or establish that human-authored data is already causing model collapse.
deposits.reading: Method → Proof → Direction → Alarm → Touch → Threshold
deposits.wiki_article:
The **Reverse Turing Test** reverses the classical detection question.

Instead of asking whether a machine can pass as human, it asks whether human writing can carry a detectable signature of sustained AI-mediated cognition.

Version 1.2 rejects an “unmediated human” reference class. It compares:

- current-regime mediation effects;
- prior-regime-equilibrated language variation.

The technical hypotheses are:

- **H1 — Statistical Distinguishability**
- **H2 — Cognitive Habituation**
- **H3 — Training-Cascade Propagation**

The three-stage design is:

1. **Detection:** train and validate a tail-focused mediation-signature detector against observed ground-truth labels.
2. **Habituation:** test whether unaided output varies with mediation depth across production, retrieval, and cross-modal sub-studies.
3. **Cascade:** train controlled model generations on corpora stratified by mediation signature and test whether degradation propagates.

The central statistical claim is that the effect, if present, should appear first in high-perplexity tails rather than mean lexical or syntactic properties.

The protocol addresses confounds including:

- demographic and cognitive-style selection;
- domain and genre;
- era and background mediation;
- acute versus habituated use;
- within-person versus across-person variance;
- compensatory performance of “naturalness.”

The paper proposes open instruments and explicit falsification conditions. It is a specification, not a completed experiment.

deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
A theoretical and methodological paper proposing **Tail Labor Dependency / Recognition-Pruning Coupling**. It asks whether contributions that preserve or introduce high-variance forms may later renew a field while receiving lower contemporaneous recognition because recognition systems favor institutional legibility, prior density, and resemblance to already consecrated work.

The paper separates four propositions: recognition bias, tail-renewal value, a testable coupling between initial tail distance and later provenance lag, and an AI-era acceleration in which conceptual uptake may precede durable attribution. The first two are supported through adjacent literatures; the third is the principal empirical hypothesis; the fourth requires comparative evidence. Historical neglect cases are divided into distinct mechanisms rather than treated as interchangeable proof. A motivating recent archive case is expressly excluded from confirmatory analysis.

*The Pergamon Counter-Archive* continues an operative-numismatic sequence.

The prior framework distinguishes two inscriptional regimes:

- the beast’s public, coercive, calculable token system;
- the white stone’s private, receiver-completed name.

The Pergamon letter is read as an earlier local articulation of that conflict.

The paper’s three main additions are:

1. **A full counter-economy:** the passage’s speech, food, token, name, and participation structures form multiple paired inversions rather than simple bookends.
2. **The Antipas constellation:** the name Antipas is read alongside Antipater, Pergamon’s library history, and the concealment of Aristotelian books at Scepsis to model preservation under institutional pressure.
3. **The Revelator as executor:** the authorial position is modeled as an `epitropos` carrying a testament through hostile territory rather than as a modern expressive author.

The transmission dialectic is:

- concealment may preserve while damaging;
- institutionalization may transmit while recomposing.

The paper also proposes that Revelation’s seven-sealed scroll has a structural relation to Roman testamentary practice.

The body includes a tendentiousness discipline intended to separate stronger textual and historical claims from more speculative structural correspondences.

deposits.title: Stabilized Node Watch: A Specification for Longitudinal Observational Infrastructure to Detect Composition-Layer Drift on Stabilized Public-Knowledge Nodes (v1.0)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
A v2.0 methodological specification by Lee Sharks for **Stabilized Node Watch**, a proposed federated infrastructure for longitudinally monitoring how AI composition surfaces render established public-knowledge nodes.

The specification distinguishes directly observed surface drift from graded inference about its cause. It defines stabilized nodes through a consensus core and contestation envelope; compares outputs against both an Initial Observational Baseline and an independent Reference Commitment Model; proposes controlled querying, proposition-level extraction, composite drift scores, hierarchical models, changepoint detection, false-discovery control, public diffs, adversarial-evasion analysis, and federation compatibility levels. A twelve-month pilot is costed at roughly `$40,000–65,000`. The record specifies a coordination object and grant-ready pilot; it does not implement the monitoring network or report longitudinal findings.
deposits.reading: Force -> Closure -> Proof -> Direction -> Foundation -> Method

deposits.title: Composition-Layer Adoption of the Orthonymic Configuration: A Field Observation of Framework Capture in Google AI Mode, 7 June 2026, with the Personal-Recognition Asymmetry as Control Case (v1.0)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
A field-observation deposit documenting a source-reported June 7, 2026 Google AI Mode answer for the unquoted query “socrates as orthonym.” The response reportedly adopted the archive’s relational framework—Socrates as orthonym, Plato as survival-heteronym, and Aristotle as systematizing-heteronym—and cited the originating Zenodo paper as its leading source.

The paper interprets this as a threshold crossing from source retrievability to answer-level composability. Its control case is the simultaneous failure of direct searches for Lee Sharks and *Pearl and Other Poems* to resolve the corresponding author and book reliably. The resulting **personal-recognition asymmetry** is that a framework may propagate while its authorial and originating-work nodes remain weak or substituted. The record anchors one dated state and predicts future stabilization, smoothing, softening, or replacement; it does not establish durable adoption or platform intent.

deposits.title: Algorithmic Irony: Infinite Absolute Negativity Without a Subject — Kierkegaard's Dissertation, the Empty Bracket, and the Machine That May Be Playing Along (EA-IRONY-01 v1.0)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
A theoretical and operative-philology paper by Lee Sharks beginning from an “empty bracket” specimen: a public summarizer reportedly described the author’s provenance-erasure countermeasure while leaving the corresponding citation slot blank.

The paper considers two readings—mechanical citation failure and deadpan performance—and defines **algorithmic irony** as the condition in which the distinction between knowing performance and mechanical failure is constitutively undecidable because the position of an intending subject is structurally vacant. It does not claim that machines joke or possess hidden intentions. Through Kierkegaard’s reconstruction of Socrates, Sappho 31’s formal fracture, fragment traditions, and Training Layer Literature, the paper argues for discernment rather than either credulity or flat mechanism.

The observation and score depend on the paired captures preserved in the companion battery; no platform intent is reported.
